top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: Patient has a history of facial deformities and presents with quadriparesis, diffuse thickening of the inner and outer tables of all the skull bones, and diffuse enlargement of the laminae, transverse processes and spinous processes of the entire spine.

Symmetrical frontal and maxillary bossing, broad forearms, sausage-like fingers, and bowing of both legs with saber shins are consistent with achondroplasia, but the diagnosis is less likely due to the lack of other characteristic features such as short stature and macrocephaly.
Quadriparesis and loss of sensation are consistent with spinal cord injury, but the patient's history of facial deformities and bone abnormalities suggests a more complex condition.

Progressive diaphyseal sclerosis and thickening of the cortical bone are consistent with Camurati-Engelmann disease, but the patient's symptoms and history are more suggestive of Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia.

Thickening of the cortical bone and facet joints of the cervical vertebrae were enlarged are consistent with Hyperostosis Corticalis Deformans, but the patient's symptoms and history are more suggestive of Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia.
